essence.one_sentence: On a dark surface a status pill is judged by what a glance can read, and very compact is a family of widgets: the same tracker counted in pixels, in visible words, in rows, or in actions in view.
essence.summary: A dark one-line status pill that opens from its own anchor into a tracking menu; the glance and the menu share one surface.

formula.full: dark tinted pill + stage word and ETA + menu opened from the same anchor + timeline of scans + live status announcement
formula.essential: pill that opens into a timeline menu

roles.live region: the status heard, not only seen

angles.text: One stage word and one number carry the status; the rest of the widget waits until someone asks for it.
The menu is a vertical record of scans, read top to bottom with the current scan marked, opened from the pill.
The open menu steps one lightness band up from the pill, so depth reads as light on dark instead of a shadow.
A toast that does not leave on its own: the notice reading and the tracker reading meet in one persistent pill.
Several parcels as offset, scaled-down layers, the way stacked toasts fan out, each keeping its own stage word.

poles: one stage word and one number
lighter layers for depth on dark
muted text held at 4.5:1 or more on the top raised step, which caps how light that step can go
13 px detail rows at high contrast

llm_brief.text: On the table: the user's words, quoted: “dark mode”, “very compact”, “collapsible”, “toast UI menu”, “menu”, “tracking a package”. Measured and sourced: primary text #F2F3F5 holds 15.2 to 16.4:1 on the base band; muted text #959BA6 holds 6.0 to 6.5:1 on the base bands and 4.9:1 on the top raised step; touch targets 24 CSS px at AA and 44 at enhanced, with Apple at 44pt and Material at 48dp; the stage words are label created, in transit, out for delivery, delivered and exception. Very compact reads several ways, side by side: by size (a 24 to 31 px pill, a 32 to 44 px line, a 56 to 72 px row, a 240 to 320 px panel, a round count chip) or by content (2 to 12 words, 1 to 6 rows, 0 to 3 actions in view). Deep cuts from the pools: Pebble timeline pins, airline departure-board flip tiles, a postal sorting-office tally sheet, a container manifest seal, a lit control panel in a dark cockpit, a cinema after the lights drop, a palm webOS card stack. Ways in: read at arm's length, one stage word and one number; timeline as the body, a vertical record of scans opened from the pill; lighter layer, the open menu one lightness band above the pill; notice that stays, the notice and the tracker in one persistent pill; parcels stacked, offset layers each with its own stage word. Dials: pill height 32 to 44 px for one line, or 56 to 72 px for a dense row; pill radius 16 to 22 px, or a fixed 999 px that tolerates height changes; panel radius 12 px reads tight and utilitarian, 20 px reads soft; hairline 1 px or 1.5 px, the heavier one reading heavy at compact sizes; collapse motion short and crisp, middle and springy, or long and linear, each a different feel; auto-close timer 4000 ms as the sourced default, overridable per notice. Worn paths: the usual move is a full-page modal; fresher: a corner-anchored toast that leaves the page scrollable, with the open menu drawn over its own footprint. The usual move is a generic gray card with a progress bar; fresher: a near-black pill, or a one-row card with the ETA as the headline number. The usual move is a full-width banner; fresher: a compact pill that sizes to its content and opens from the same anchor. The usual move is a light theme with a dark tint; fresher: deep blue-ink layers stacked lighter, light text at high contrast, and one saturated status accent. The usual move is 8 px microtext; fresher: 13 px detail rows at 1.5 line height. Open: whether tracking data is live or mocked (assumed: mocked, shaped like a carrier timeline, no network calls); one package or several (assumed: one, with several as a reading); Apple's own spring values were not found in fetched pages (assumed: a spread of curves); whether loading, delivered and network-error states appear on the source pages (not resolvable from them).

ak-light-tint.instead: deep blue-ink surfaces built as stacked lighter layers, with light text at high contrast and one saturated status accent

k-dark-surface.text: Does every surface of the tracker sit on a dark, tinted neutral, with no light page or white card behind it?

test.spec: pill and open-menu backgrounds are dark tinted neutrals; no white card anywhere in the widget

k-compact.text: Does the collapsed tracker read as a pill about 24 to 44 px tall, a row about 56 to 72 px tall, or a count chip, with its stage word or number in view?

test.spec: collapsed bounding-box height in px; 24 to 44 for a pill, 56 to 72 for a row, one number for a chip

k-collapsible.text: Does one control expand the tracker into its menu and collapse it back again?

test.spec: activate the control open and closed; the menu appears and disappears, and the control's state changes with it

k-toast.text: Does the surface read as a small notice floating over the page, without taking focus when it appears?

test.spec: on appearance, the active element is the same as before the widget appeared

k-menu.text: Does the expanded state list tracking details as rows a reader can scan from top to bottom?

test.spec: expanded menu shows a row per detail, in reading order, with a consistent left edge

k-tracking.text: Does the tracker name one package's current stage and its expected arrival?

test.spec: the collapsed state shows a stage word; the menu shows a time or an ETA

k-theme.text: Does the dark palette apply when no theme is chosen, and does a light or dark setting override it?

test.spec: prefers-color-scheme: dark block sets the tokens; a data-theme attribute overrides it

k-aria-expanded.text: Does the toggle expose aria-expanded that matches whether the menu is visible?

test.spec: toggle carries aria-expanded="true" or "false" and changes with the menu

k-live-status.text: Does a status change get announced through a live region or a status role?

test.spec: role="status" or aria-live appears on the element that changes, count of at least 1

k-contrast-text.text: Does each text label clear 4.5:1 against the lightest surface it sits on, including the muted tier on the top raised step?

test.spec: WCAG relative-luminance ratio for primary, secondary and muted text against its surface; muted #959BA6 against the top raised step #2C2D36 at 4.5:1 or more

k-status-glyph.text: Does each status carry a glyph and a short word as well as its colour?

test.spec: remove the colour in a greyscale render; every status is still named

k-states.text: Does each tracker state (empty, loading, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, exception) get a visible answer on screen?

test.spec: render each state; none is blank or unlabelled

k-reduced-motion.text: When reduced motion is requested, does the expand and collapse still change state in place, without travel?

test.spec: emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; the menu still opens and closes, without sliding or morphing

k-target-size.text: Are pointer targets at least 24 CSS px, and 44 px at the enhanced level?

test.spec: smallest side of the toggle and each action button, in CSS px

k-no-noise-words.text: Does the copy leave out filler words such as stunning, seamless, sleek, modern and premium?

test.spec: \b(stunning|seamless|sleek|modern|premium)\b, count of 0

k-no-gray-card.text: Does the tracker read as more than a generic gray card with a progress bar?

test.spec: the collapsed pill or row has a stage word and an ETA as its headline, not only a bar

k-no-blocking-modal.text: Does the page behind the open tracker stay scrollable and clickable?

test.spec: with the menu open, scroll the page and click an element behind the widget; both respond

k-no-full-banner.text: Does the tracker size to its content as a pill or card, rather than a full-width strip?

test.spec: widget width in px against the viewport width; a strip spans the viewport

k-type-floor.text: Are the smallest labels at 12 px or more, with detail rows at 13 px and a line height near 1.5?

test.spec: smallest computed font-size of text nodes in px; detail-row line height as a ratio

k-morph-anchor.text: Does the expanded state grow from the same edge the pill is pinned to?

test.spec: the anchor edge stays fixed across collapse and expand in captured frames

k-stage-words.text: Where does each stage's word come from in the shared carrier set, and is it the same word in the pill and in the menu?

test.spec: compare the stage word in the collapsed state with the matching row in the menu

k-exception-way-back.text: Does the exception state offer a next step on screen: a carrier link, a copy control, or a refresh?

test.spec: render the exception state; at least one of open-carrier, copy-number or refresh is reachable from it

q-data.text: Is tracking data live or mocked?
q-data.default: mocked data shaped like a carrier timeline, no network calls

q-stack.default: one package in the widget; several as readings

q-apple-spring.text: Apple's own spring values for expand and collapse were not found in fetched pages.
q-apple-spring.default: use a spread, not a single curve

q-collapse-impl.text: Implement collapse with CSS transitions, WAAPI, or a JS spring library?
q-collapse-impl.default: CSS transitions on transform and opacity, with the spring approximated by a cubic-bezier with a small overshoot
q-collapse-impl.impact: how the spring feels and whether retargeting mid-motion is smooth

q-material-snackbar.text: Figures taken from search snippets or memory, not fetched pages: Material 48dp single-line snackbar height, the Material dark base #121212, WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 non-text contrast, and WCAG 2.4.7 focus visible.
q-material-snackbar.default: treat each as inferred until checked
q-material-snackbar.impact: pill height, dark base, contrast floor and focus ring
q-material-snackbar.resolve: fetch the pages or render with --render

q-dark-mode.text: Does the block ship a dark-mode variant of its own colours? Its page text does not mention dark mode or theme, and the preview shows only the site's dark background.
q-dark-mode.default: not shown on the page; unknown
q-dark-mode.resolve: inspect the installed code (Pro, not fetched)

q-loading-delivered.text: Are loading, delivered and network-error states shown? The carrier labels 'Accepted' and 'delayed' come from search snippets and naming habits, not from a fetched page.

q-toast-timer.text: Auto-dismiss duration for the notice reading
q-toast-timer.default: no default: the timer belongs to the auto-dismiss reading only; goey-toast's 4000 ms is one value to test among others

p-dark.text: The widget is in dark mode.

p-collapsible.text: The widget can collapse and expand.

p-toast.text: The UI is a toast: a small notification-style surface.

p-menu.text: The toast is also a menu of options and details.

p-tracking.text: Its job is tracking a package.

p-whole.term: dark compact collapsible toast menu for tracking a package
p-whole.anchor: a dark mode, very compact collapsible toast UI menu for tracking a package
p-whole.text: A dark-mode, very compact, collapsible toast-style UI menu that tracks one package.

pr-visibility.text: Nielsen heuristic 1: the interface keeps the user informed of what is going on, through feedback within a reasonable time.
behaviors: The collapsed pill shows the current stage (in transit, out for delivery) without any click.
Refreshing or loading shows a progress indicator inside the pill, not a blank surface.
A color or icon change confirms that a tap registered before the panel opens.
pr-visibility.principle: Users who can see the current state feel in control and can decide their next step.

pr-disclosure.text: A disclosure widget collapses and expands content; a button controls a section that is hidden by default.
behaviors: Only the summary line is visible until the user opens the menu.
The arrow or chevron flips direction to show the state: right when hidden, down when open.
Tracking details (timeline, ETA, actions) stay hidden until the menu opens.
pr-disclosure.principle: Show the summary first and put detail behind one deliberate action, so the default view stays small.

pr-aria-expanded.text: The toggle is a button, and its aria-expanded value tracks whether the controlled content is visible.
behaviors: The pill is a real button; aria-expanded flips between true and false on each toggle.
aria-controls points at the menu element, so assistive technology can find the panel.
The label can stay constant (for example a tracking label) because aria-expanded carries the state.
pr-aria-expanded.principle: Expanded state must be exposed to the accessibility tree, not only shown by an arrow.

pr-status-live.term: status messages in a live region
pr-status-live.text: Status changes that do not take focus are announced to assistive technology through a live region or status role.
behaviors: A change to the stage label (in transit to out for delivery) is announced in a polite live region.
Routine refreshes with no change are not announced, so the screen reader is not chatty.
Expanding or collapsing the menu is not announced as a status message; aria-expanded covers it.
pr-status-live.principle: Status messages are for the user who cannot see a change; announce only what changed and do so without stealing focus.

pr-contrast.term: text and surface contrast on dark
pr-contrast.text: Text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background, or 3:1 when it is large text.
behaviors: Small status labels (12 to 13px) on a dark pill need 4.5:1; only text at large sizes may drop to 3:1.
Placeholder, hover and focus text need the same ratio as body text.
Light-on-dark text fails quickly when its grey is near the surface grey; check the pair, not the palette.
pr-contrast.principle: Contrast protects readers with moderately low vision and reduced contrast sensitivity.
signals: muted grey label on dark pill

pr-reduced-motion.text: The prefers-reduced-motion query tells the page that the user has asked the device to minimize non-essential motion.
behaviors: Under reduce, the pill-to-menu morph becomes a fade or an instant change; the content still appears.
Scaling or panning large objects is the usual vestibular trigger, so the morph should avoid large movement.
The query can be checked in CSS and in matchMedia with the same string; theme switching is separate from motion.
pr-reduced-motion.principle: Motion that is not needed to understand the state should be removed or replaced for users who asked.

pr-aria-expanded-readings.text: The expanded state can be exposed as a disclosure button, as a menu pattern, or as a live-region announcement. The three are side by side; none is the default.

readings.in_practice: A button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the menu's controls sit in normal tab order.
role=menu with arrow-key movement between menuitems, and focus managed inside the menu.
No expanded state on the control; each open or close is announced in a polite live region.

pr-focus-target.text: Keyboard focus needs a visible ring, and pointer targets keep the sizes set in target size. Where focus lands when the menu opens has its own readings in pr-focus-open.
behaviors: The pill and each menu row show a visible focus ring that is more than a colour change
Small icon buttons inside the menu keep a 24 by 24 CSS px target, or spacing that gives the same area
pr-focus-target.principle: Keyboard users and users with motor limits need to see where they are and hit small controls reliably.

pr-focus-open.text: When the menu opens, focus can move into it, stay on the pill, or depend on how it was opened. The three are side by side; none is the default.

readings.in_practice: On open, focus moves to the first menu control; on close, focus returns to the pill.
signals: focus on the first menu control

readings.in_practice: Focus does not move; the menu is linked to the pill through aria-controls, and the change is announced in a live region.
A keyboard open moves focus into the menu; a pointer open leaves focus on the pill.

specifics._about: Specific rungs for a compact package-tracking pill: status words, timeline layout, sizes, timings. Sourced values are quoted; illustrative values are spreads for the builder to choose from.

target_size.text: Pointer targets need 24 CSS px at AA and 44 at enhanced; Apple uses 44pt and Material 48dp.

status_vocabulary.text: Carriers share a short status set; names differ by carrier, and one label per state keeps a pill readable.
behaviors: A stall after 'Label Created' (48+ hours with no scan) is a warehouse delay; an 'Exception' is an interruption, not a loss

toast_stacking.text: Stacked toasts offset each item by its index and scale it down for depth; the transition is interruptible.
behaviors: CSS keyframes break when toasts are added mid-animation; a transition on transform does not
A single pill has one item, so the stack itself does not transfer; the offset and the scale per index do

exemplars._about: Candidate-style facets. Unverified leads are never recommendations.

ex-just-sonner.reading: deck that fans out on pointer hover
ex-just-sonner.text: Lead from a search snippet only: a deck that collapses and fans out, pausing while the pointer stays. Check before using.

widget_anatomy._about: Anatomy, states and compact variants of the tracker pill and menu. Readings are side by side; none is the default.

options._about: options, not requirements: decisions the build has to make. Each lists what it fits and what it costs.

opt-morph-vs-slide.decision: How the pill becomes the menu

options.option: morph: the pill grows from its anchor
options.fits_when: one shared surface and short content

options.option: slide: the panel slides out from an edge beside the pill
options.fits_when: more content than a pill holds; costs a second element to keep in sync

opt-auto-vs-persistent.decision: Whether the widget leaves on a timer

options.option: auto-dismiss on a timer, pause on hover
options.fits_when: a notice about a single event
tracking that runs for days; costs screen space the whole time
the ETA is the one thing glanced at
the ETA sits beside a timeline that explains it

opt-stack.decision: How many packages one widget holds

options.option: stacked, offset by index and scaled down
options.fits_when: several packages; costs height and read order

options.option: fixed to a corner over any page
options.fits_when: a status that should follow the user
the status belongs to one piece of content

island-states.term: island states: pill, capsule, split, full
island-states.text: The page names four island states plus a none state, held as one enum that drives every transition.
properties: Split: island divides into two parts
behaviors: Each state is a discrete enum value, so the island animates between named states rather than free sizes
Split is the only state that changes the outline's shape, not just its width
island-states.principle: A small fixed set of named states keeps the morph predictable.
signals: one enum with a None value

island-visual-pill.term: pill as seen in the page
island-visual-pill.text: The screenshot shows a dark pill with a caller's avatar, a timer, a name and a red round button, sitting in a phone frame's top cutout.
behaviors: The pill holds one line of status plus one action in a single dark bar
island-visual-pill.principle: Status plus one action is enough for the compact state.
signals: black capsule at top of screen

wa-toast.text: Toast can mean a notice that leaves on its own or a surface that stays until something ends it. Each reading holds the same word differently.

readings.in_practice: Appears, holds on a timer, then leaves. Goey-toast closes after 4000 ms by default, and per-toast duration overrides it.
One pill anchored to a corner with no timer. It stays while the package is in transit and leaves when delivered or closed by hand.
One item per package, each offset by its index and scaled down for depth, with the transition interruptible.

wa-anatomy.text: Collapsed and expanded states share one surface and one anchor; the content inside is swapped. The pill carries the headline and one action, and the menu carries the timeline, ETA and actions.
behaviors: Expanding grows the same surface from its anchor edge rather than swapping in a second element
Status plus one action is enough for the compact state
wa-anatomy.principle: One surface that changes shape keeps the user oriented about where the menu came from.
signals: same anchor edge in both states
one action in the collapsed state

wa-precedents.text: Three precedents each answer one piece of this widget: a pill that morphs into a body, an island with named states, and a chat shipping tracker that lays out scan states as a timeline.
behaviors: The goey-toast blob grows away from the edge the toast is pinned to
The island moves between named states rather than free sizes
The shipping tracker marks each scan state with a glyph and a word, never colour alone
wa-precedents.principle: Each precedent is a part to borrow, not a whole widget to copy.
signals: check, ring and hollow dot glyphs

wa-states.text: Six states need a visual answer: empty, loading, in transit, out for delivery, delivered and exception. A state with no answer on screen reads as a bug.

readings.in_practice: When the package is delivered the pill leaves by itself.
The pill shows Delivered and stays until dismissed; the menu keeps the full scan history, newest first.

behaviors: Each state has a glyph and a word, so colour adds emphasis on top of them
wa-states.principle: Every state gets a glyph, a word and a slot; a blank pill is a failure state.
signals: one glyph and one word per state
empty and loading share the same slot

wa-act.text: From the open menu the user copies the tracking number or opens the carrier's tracking page.
properties: carrier name in the link text
behaviors: Copy puts the tracking number on the clipboard and the button label changes to Copied for a short time
The Copied label is announced in a polite live region
Open carrier opens the carrier's tracking page for this number in a new tab, with the carrier named in the link text
wa-act.principle: The act step sits in the menu, so the compact pill keeps one action at most.

wa-dismiss.text: The user gets back from the open menu by collapsing it into the pill, or by dismissing the widget. The two are side by side.

readings.in_practice: The menu closes back into the pill; the pill keeps the stage word and ETA, and focus returns to the pill.
A close control hides the widget; the next status change brings it back.

wa-exception-way-back.term: exception state and its way back
wa-exception-way-back.text: The exception state gives a way back: open the carrier page, copy the number to raise it with the carrier, or ask for the status again.
behaviors: The exception row keeps its glyph, its word and the open-carrier link
Asking again refreshes the status and announces the result in a polite live region
Exception does not end persistence, so the widget stays until the status changes or the user dismisses it
wa-exception-way-back.principle: An error state that offers no next step is a dead end.

wa-compact.text: Very compact can be read first by size: a pill, a row, a panel or a chip. Each size is a different widget; words, rows and actions sit in wa-compact-content.

readings.in_practice: A 24 to 31 px pill: one dot and one stage word, at the 24 px pointer floor.
One line: a status dot, a short stage word, at most one action.
Icon, stage label and ETA side by side at 12 to 13px; the rest sits behind the tap.
Stacked timeline rows at 12 to 13px, one scan event per row, in a 240 to 320px panel.
A round chip with one number, such as days to delivery; the rest sits behind the tap.

wa-compact-content.text: Very compact can also be read by what is visible: a few words, a few rows, a few actions, with the rest behind the tap. Each amount is a different widget.

readings.in_practice: Two to twelve words visible: the stage word and ETA in the pill, a few more words per row in the menu, and the rest behind the tap.
One row visible in the collapsed state; one to six rows in the open menu, with the timeline scrolling past six.
Zero to three action controls visible: none to one in the pill, two or three in the menu.

wa-failures.term: common failures of compact dark widgets
wa-failures.text: Compact dark widgets fail in four checkable ways; a clean dark look is judged alongside them.

failure_modes.mode: text under 4.5:1 on a dark surface
failure_modes.check: each text pair on its lightest surface

failure_modes.mode: status change with no live region

failure_modes.check: expanded state in the accessibility tree

wa-failures.principle: Compact makes the failures small and easy to miss, so they are checked on purpose.
signals: status change with no live region

collapse_motion._about: Options and readings, not requirements: how the collapsed pill opens into the detail panel and back. Sourced spring values come from the Dynamic Island write-up; every duration and curve below is illustrative.

island-split-spring.text: The split morph runs a spring whose stiffness and damping switch with the split state, with mass fixed at 2.
behaviors: Splitting uses the stiffer, less damped spring, so it snaps open with a little overshoot
Returning from split uses the softer, more damped spring, so it settles without bounce
island-split-spring.principle: Stiffness and damping are swapped per target state rather than one spring for both directions.

island-split-widths.text: The page sets the left side's width target to 62 for split and back to 32 otherwise, with a 100 ms delay before the split width moves.
behaviors: The morph value and the width are driven separately, so the path can change shape before the side widens
island-split-widths.principle: Stagger the shape morph and the width change so the split reads as two steps.

cm-transform-only.text: Animate transform and opacity; treat width, height and top as state changes you fake with transforms, so the motion does not force layout on each frame.
behaviors: Scaling the pill toward the panel distorts text, so swap to real layout after the scale settles or fade the content across the swap
A height reveal that cannot be done with transform can use clip-path inset, which stays on the compositor
Animating the shadow mid-motion is a common stutter source; fix the shadow and move only the surface

cm-toast-enter-exit.text: The compact pill enters and leaves as its own motion, separate from the panel's open and close.
behaviors: Enter from the anchor edge with a short spring; a 200 ms ease-out feels abrupt, 350 ms reads as deliberate
Exit shorter than enter, so leaving does not hold attention
Auto-close after 4000 ms is the toast default; a tracker pill may hold longer or stay until the user collapses it
Hover or focus pauses the auto-close timer

cm-collapsible.text: 'Collapsible' can mean the container morphs, the body folds in its frame, the panel slides from an edge, or it toggles at once. Each reads differently in motion.

readings.in_practice: The pill stretches into the panel from one anchor in one spring; rows arrive after the shape settles.
The top edge stays pinned under the pill and the body grows downward, rows unfolding with a 30 to 60 ms stagger.
The panel travels one panel-width from a screen edge over a dim scrim; the pill stays put.
Two layers swap in one frame; aria-expanded flips as the panel appears.

cm-timing-spread.text: Duration and curve are one pair: short and crisp, middle and springy, long and linear. Several values far apart, each with what it does.
behaviors: 150 ms ease-out: quick and quiet, reads as a snap; fits a tight pill that opens a short list
280 ms spring with a small overshoot (stiffness near 120 to 180, damping near 30 to 50): the outline briefly passes its target before settling; the Dynamic Island split values sit in this family
450 ms linear fold: slow and even, the motion is legible step by step; can feel sluggish if the panel is tall
Split and unsplit use different spring damping on the same morph, so opening overshoots and closing does not
Collapse can run shorter than expand: about 180 to 300 ms against 250 to 400 ms

cm-interrupt.text: A tap during the open motion retargets the same spring instead of waiting for it to finish.
behaviors: Reversing mid-expand starts the spring from its current velocity, so the motion bends back rather than jumping
The retarget keeps the anchor fixed, so the pill returns to where it was
Rows already revealed fade out first, then the shape closes; content does not land on a moving edge

island-content-transition.term: content fade and blur per state
island-content-transition.text: Incoming content fades in with an 8px blur-to-sharp, delayed past the island's switch time, while the status bar blurs and dims when the island is active.
behaviors: Content waits for the shape to settle before it appears, so text does not land on a moving edge
island-content-transition.principle: Content enters after the container settles.

opt-interrupt.decision: What a tap during the open or close motion does

options.option: retarget the same spring from its current velocity, anchor fixed
options.fits_when: the motion should bend back and feel continuous

options.option: reverse mid-flight on an ease-out curve, velocity not carried over
options.fits_when: a quick, predictable reversal; costs a visible jump in speed

options.option: queue the tap until the motion settles
options.fits_when: content needs to finish landing before the next change; costs a delay the user can feel as lag

options.option: snap to the target state at once
options.fits_when: reduced motion, or a status change that cannot wait; costs the continuity of the morph

pill-to-toast-transfer.term: what transfers to a compact collapsible toast
pill-to-toast-transfer.text: The pill-to-full pattern maps to a compact toast that grows into a tracking menu from the same anchor.
properties: content fades in after shape settles
behaviors: A toast that stays put and grows keeps its position in the user's eye
Splitting into two parts is one option for showing two statuses side by side
pill-to-toast-transfer.principle: Separate the container's motion from the content's motion.
signals: compact pill grows into a panel
content appears after the frame settles

gm-states.text: A toast starts as a pill and expands into a blob when a description is given; a success action can morph the blob back to a pill.
behaviors: Pill shows the headline only (Default, Success, Error, Warning, Info).
Passing a description or ReactNode body grows the pill into a blob holding the body.
An action with successLabel morphs the expanded blob back to a pill on click.
Center positions grow the body outward from the pill; right-side positions mirror the blob horizontally.
gm-states.principle: The collapsed state carries the headline; the expanded state carries detail; the same surface changes shape rather than swapping.

gm-anchor.text: The morph direction depends on the toast's screen position, so the blob grows away from the edge it is pinned to.
behaviors: Right-side positions auto-mirror the blob horizontally.
Center positions use a symmetric morph from the pill.
Six positions: top and bottom, left, center and right.
gm-anchor.principle: Anchor the morph to the edge so the expanding body never runs off-screen.

gm-states-readings.text: The expansion can be read as a morph of one surface, a static card swap, or a panel that slides out beside the pill. gm-states keeps the sampled morph. The three are side by side; none is the default.

readings.in_practice: The pill grows into a body from the same surface; the shape changes rather than the content swapping.
A second card appears in place of the pill and the pill is removed; no shape is shared.
signals: swap in one frame or fade

readings.in_practice: A panel travels out from an edge beside the pill, which stays in place.

gt-duration.text: Toasts auto-close after a timer; the default display duration is 4000 ms and can be overridden per toast or per toaster.
behaviors: Default auto-close after 4000 ms.
Per-toast duration overrides the toaster default.
onAutoClose fires only on timer close; onDismiss fires for any dismissal.
gt-duration.principle: A status toast should leave on its own timer unless the user needs it to stay, which matches a transient notice rather than a persistent tracker.

gt-spring.text: Spring on uses a bounce-tuned curve for the landing squish, blob morph, pill resize and header squish; spring off replaces all of them with smooth ease-in-out.
behaviors: bounce defaults to 0.4 and ranges from 0.05 (subtle) to 0.8 (dramatic).
presets smooth, bouncy, subtle and snappy name whole timing sets.
Error shake keeps running even when spring is off.
gt-spring.principle: Bounce is a single knob; turning spring off gives a calm ease-in-out morph without changing the layout.

gt-duration-readings.text: Display duration can be read as a timer that closes the toast, a timer that restarts on each update, or a persistent state with no timer. gt-duration keeps the sourced timer fact.

readings.in_practice: The toast closes after a set time (4000 ms in the sampled library), and a per-toast value overrides the default.
Each status change restarts the timer, so the widget leaves a set time after the last change.
No timer; the widget stays while the package is in transit and leaves when it is delivered.
No timer; the widget stays until the user dismisses it, whatever the status.

gd-theme.text: The toaster has a theme option with light and dark values, defaulting to light; the blob fill is set per toast.
behaviors: theme light or dark, default light.
fillColor sets the blob background per toast; the docs sample uses a dark navy fill with a dark grey border.
borderWidth defaults to 1.5 px.
gd-theme.principle: Dark is a theme switch plus explicit fill and border colors, not a separate component.

gd-visual.term: visual read of the demo surfaces
gd-visual.text: The rendered page is light: a warm off-white page, white cards with thin borders and a dark text color; the dark theme is only reachable through the builder toggle.
behaviors: Builder panel has a light and dark toggle beside a Fill Color field and Border controls.
The dark variant's surface colors are not shown in the captured page; no hex values for the dark theme are visible on the page.
gd-visual.principle: The page itself gives no dark surface values; treat the dark fill as a sample, not a token set.

status_timeline._about: Shipping tracker block (shadcn.io, Radix UI): how the status timeline is laid out and worded. Found online.

ls-states-handled.text: Empty field, malformed number, unknown number and known number are the four input states; each has a fixed reply, and only known numbers post a card.
behaviors: A malformed number shows the problem under the field and posts nothing
ls-states-handled.principle: Every input state has an answer, so nothing is left blank.
signals: reserved error line under the field
No such number in this demo

ls-demo-limits.text: Scans and times are fixed sample data in the file; the switch only adds a log line, with no lookup and no alert.
behaviors: Real use needs a carrier API call in one function
ls-demo-limits.principle: The demo shows the layout; the data source is a separate seam.
signals: three sample tracking numbers as buttons

ls-timeline-layout.text: Scan events in a vertical ordered list inside a fixed-height frame; each state gets a glyph and a short word, and the current scan is marked Now.
behaviors: Only the log scrolls; the frame keeps its height
A future scan shows Expected before its time
Each state carries a glyph and a word; the current row is marked as the current step for screen readers
ls-timeline-layout.principle: A fixed frame and fixed words keep a short timeline readable while scans arrive.

precedents._about: Images the moodboard looked at and that bear on a dark, compact tracking toast. Found online, not user-supplied.

signals: single bordered input with monospace number
three-row list of carriers with pill buttons
mb-desc-tracking-entry.text: A dark card with a mono tracking field and a list of carrier rows, each with a small initials badge and a ghost button.

mb-desc-order-timeline.term: dark order card with four-step timeline
signals: step title and date on two lines
mb-desc-order-timeline.text: A compact order panel where the current step is a numbered ring and completed steps are checks joined by a thin vertical line.

mb-desc-map-steps.term: dark step list beside a map
signals: Last scan and Expected tags on the right edge
current step as a filled white dot
mb-desc-map-steps.text: A narrow dark step list with right-aligned Last scan and Expected tags, next to a map showing the parcel.

mb-desc-chat-order.term: dark chat with compact order side panel
signals: side panel with order number and status pill
four steps with check, ring and open circle
date line under each step title
mb-desc-chat-order.text: A chat window with an order panel at the right whose four steps reuse the same marker set as the card.

mb-desc-block-docs.term: dark docs page with framed five-scan tracker
signals: fixed-height framed window with a header row
five scan rows with check marks
Now marker on the newest scan
mb-desc-block-docs.text: The shipping tracker block shown on a dark docs page: a bordered bot card with a header, then a scrolling list of scans in a fixed frame.

mb-desc-pill-morph.term: dark write-up with pill, capsule, split and full island states
signals: black page with a rounded phone frame
enum of Pill, Capsule, Split, Full states
mb-desc-pill-morph.text: A dark tutorial page for a dynamic-island widget: the pill is the default compact state and expands through capsule and split states into a full panel.

skipped.reason: light toast docs screenshot; precedent is light, not dark
WCAG target-size figure, accessibility not visual
ARIA disclosure diagram, light; used for accessibility, not look
light goey-toast docs page; only the overview was looked at

mb-skipped.text: Collected, looked at, and left out: light pages and diagrams, WCAG figures, author photos and illustrations.

shared_look._about: What the dark tracking precedents share. Visual reading of six images, not a measurement.

mb-density.term: dense rows with one primary line
properties: one primary status line at the largest size
secondary date or note under each row
rows divided by hairlines, not gaps
behaviors: The current state is the first row and the only bright text
Long history scrolls inside the frame; the frame keeps its height
mb-density.principle: Show the current state first and keep history quiet until asked.

mb-type.term: small type with one mono field
properties: helper and date text near 12 to 13 px in muted grey
tracking number in monospace with a copy icon
behaviors: The tracking number is the only monospace text, so it reads as data
Muted grey carries secondary text and stays legible on near-black
mb-type.principle: Scale comes from weight and grey steps, not from many sizes.

palette_samples._about: Pixel samples from the dark precedents. Image samples, not print or CSS values.

mb-pal-tracking-entry.text: Pixel samples from five dark precedents: canvases between #0A0A0A and #0F100D, raised steps near #272723 to #2A2C2E, lines near #383834 to #474747. Photo samples, not CSS values.

dark_surfaces._about: Dark-mode surfaces, text and status colors for the compact tracker. Hex values are illustrative spreads from one tinted-neutral family. Contrast ratios are computed from those hex values with the WCAG relative-luminance formula. Options, not a token set.

ds-radius-border.text: Pill and panel radii, and hairline widths, as spreads that change how soft the compact widget reads.
behaviors: Pill radius at half the height (16 to 22px on a 32 to 44px pill) reads as a capsule; a fixed 999px gives the same shape and tolerates height changes.
Panel radius 12px reads tight and utilitarian; 20px reads soft and rounded.
A 1px hairline separates surfaces on dark; the goey sample uses 1.5px, which reads heavier at compact sizes.
ds-radius-border.principle: Border width carries the separation that shadow cannot on dark, so small changes in it are visible.

ds-scheme-switch.text: Dark tokens are set under the prefers-color-scheme query and can be overridden by a theme attribute on the widget root.
behaviors: An @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block sets the tokens on :root; a data-theme="light" or data-theme="dark" attribute on the widget overrides the OS choice.
Setting color-scheme: dark lets the browser draw native controls and scrollbars on dark.
Theme switching is separate from reduced motion: the morph can stay while the colors change, and the reduced-motion query still applies.
ds-scheme-switch.principle: The OS query sets the default, and an explicit attribute wins so the widget can be pinned to a theme.

inv-contrast-floor.invariant: Every text label clears 4.5:1 against the surface it sits on, and every non-text part that carries state clears 3:1 against that surface.
inv-contrast-floor.variable: exact hues, lightness steps, number of raised steps, the muted tier's lightness, and the choice between dot and glyph
inv-contrast-floor.scope: all dark surfaces: pill, open menu, status rows, focus rings
inv-contrast-floor.text: Contrast floor on dark: 4.5:1 for text (WCAG 1.4.3) and 3:1 for non-text parts that carry state. The floor is checked on the lightest surface each text sits on.

ds-status-colors.term: status colors that hold on dark
ds-status-colors.text: Four status hues, each shown as a dot or word tint; the word and glyph carry the state, so colour is not the sole signal.
behaviors: In transit blue holds 5.3 to 8.8:1 on the base and raised bands
Out for delivery amber is the warmest and brightest hue, so it draws the eye first
Delivered green at full saturation glows on near-black; a softer green holds better
Exception red is the dimmest hue and sits near the floor on the top raised step, so keep it on the base band or pair it with its glyph
ds-status-colors.principle: A status hue is a label colour first; the word and glyph carry the state.

ds-surface-hex.text: Surface spreads for checking the 3:1 non-text floor: base bands and raised steps as hex values, with the status hues checked against each band.
behaviors: Every status hue in ds-status-colors clears 3:1 on each of these bands; the darker exception spread #F87171 holds 4.9:1 on #2C2D36
Test each status hue on the lightest band its glyph or dot sits on
ds-surface-hex.principle: The non-text floor is checked on the lightest band a glyph or dot sits on.

ds-elevation.text: A raised layer on dark can be a lighter step, a hairline edge, or a soft shadow; the readings sit side by side, none the default.

readings.in_practice: The open menu sits one band lighter than the pill, 2 to 6 lightness points per layer.
Each layer keeps its surface and gets a 1px hairline separating it from the layer below.
A dark shadow lifts the pill off a near-black base; it shows little there, so check it on the lightest band.

behaviors: Near-black base (#141519 to #1C1D22) reads as a surface; pure #000 reads as a hole
ds-elevation.principle: On dark, a layer is told apart by lightness, an edge or a shadow, and the widget says which.

ds-text-tiers.text: Three text tiers on dark: primary for status words, secondary for times and carrier names, muted for hints and metadata.
behaviors: Primary #F2F3F5 holds 15.2 to 16.4:1 on the base bands: the stage word in the collapsed pill
A softer primary near #E3E6EB holds 13.5 to 14.6:1 and reads less harsh at night; the stage word can take either
Secondary #B9BDC7 holds 8.9 to 9.7:1 on the base bands: the ETA and carrier line
Muted #959BA6 holds 6.0 to 6.5:1 on the base bands, 5.9 to 6.2:1 on the lower raised steps and 4.9:1 on the top one, clearing 4.5:1 on every band
At 12 to 13px the label counts as body text, so the 3:1 large-text allowance does not apply
ds-text-tiers.principle: The lowest text tier fails first, so check it on the highest surface it sits on.

lexicon._about: Brain-dump associations around the task: seed material to widen the work, not definitions. Deep cuts are marked in each list.

lx-toast.text: A toast is a small, brief, lifted notice that appears over the page without taking focus. Here it is a persistent pill that also opens.
sensory: a small lift on the shadow
metaphors: a receipt sliding out of a slot
a tap on the shoulder that stays until read
lx-toast.contribution: Brings the transient-notice expectation (short, dismissible) and the pill-to-blob morph that lets one surface carry both headline and detail.

lx-tracking.text: Following one parcel from label to doorstep, where the user wants to know the stage and the ETA, not the whole log.
sensory: the rattle of a van at the door
metaphors: a pin moving along a map route
a relay baton passed between hubs
deep_cuts: the Purolator-style scan chain of custody
lx-tracking.contribution: Brings the stage vocabulary (label created, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, exception) and the feeling of waiting that the pill should answer at a glance.

lx-dark.text: A dark surface where elevation shows as lighter layers and text is light on a tinted near-black.
sensory: the glow of a screen in a dim room
soft edge light on a dark pill
metaphors: a lit control panel in a dark cockpit
a cinema after the lights drop
deep_cuts: phosphor persistence on old CRT readouts
instrument backlight red dimming for night vision
lx-dark.contribution: Brings surface layering by lightness, avoidance of pure black, and the tinted greys that keep a dark pill from looking muddy.
